def min_probe_cost(n, tests):
    """Minimum worst-case cost of adaptively identifying the one guilty suspect.

    There are n suspects, numbered 0..n-1 (1 <= n <= 12). Exactly one of
    them is guilty, but you do not know which. tests is a list of at most
    12 available probes; each probe is a pair (cost, members) where cost
    is an int with 1 <= cost <= 10**6 and members is a strictly increasing
    list of suspect indices in 0..n-1 (possibly empty, possibly all of
    0..n-1).

    You investigate ADAPTIVELY: you choose a probe, pay its cost, and
    learn whether or not the guilty suspect is among that probe's members;
    you may then choose the next probe based on everything learned so far.
    The same probe may be run any number of times (repeats cost again but
    reveal nothing new). You stop once the answers received so far are
    consistent with only one suspect being guilty.

    Return the minimum, over all adaptive strategies, of the WORST-CASE
    total cost paid, where the worst case is taken over which suspect is
    guilty. If n == 1 the answer is 0 (no probes needed). If no strategy
    is guaranteed to identify the guilty suspect (i.e. some pair of
    suspects is contained-in or excluded-from exactly the same probes),
    return -1. The result is always an int.

    >>> min_probe_cost(2, [(5, [0])])
    5
    >>> min_probe_cost(3, [(1, [0]), (1, [1]), (1, [2])])
    2
    >>> min_probe_cost(4, [(10, [0, 1]), (1, [0]), (1, [1]), (1, [2])])
    3
    >>> min_probe_cost(3, [(1, [0, 1])])
    -1
    """
